takeaways: Every Azure customer gets free infrastructure-level DDoS protection, but it protects Azure's platform and may not mitigate moderate attacks against your specific workload.

Azure DDoS Protection comes as Network Protection, with rapid response support, cost protection and a WAF discount, or as the cheaper per-IP IP Protection, both adding adaptive tuning, metrics and logging.
Because DDoS protection only covers layers 3 and 4, a Web Application Firewall with the HTTP DDoS rule set, rate limiting and bot protection is needed to stop layer 7 attacks.
hook: Many small businesses assume Azure's built-in defenses keep their websites and APIs safe from DDoS attacks, yet moderate attacks can still take a single workload offline. This episode explains in plain English what DDoS attacks are, what the free tier covers, how Azure DDoS Protection and WAF fill the gaps, and how to build a practical layered defense.
